Kō Language Reference

A concise reference for the Kō programming language.

Basics

Comments

# This is a comment
x = 42  # This is an inline comment

Literals

42          # Int
0x1A        # Hex Int
0b1010      # Binary Int
0o77        # Octal Int
1_000_000   # Int with underscores
3.14        # Float
'A'         # Char
"hello"     # String
True        # Bool
False       # Bool
()          # Unit

Identifiers

x           # Simple identifier
my-var      # Hyphenated identifier
map-maybe   # Hyphenated identifier
_x          # Underscore prefix (valid identifier)

Operators

# Arithmetic
+ - * / %

# Comparison
== != < <= > >=

# Logical
and or not

# Pipe
|>

# Cons (list construction)
::

# String concatenation
String.append a b

# Assignment
:=

# Deref (dereference ref)
!expr

# Field access
record.field

Functions

Definition

fn add x y = x + y

fn main =
  println (add 1 2)  # 3

Multi-line Body

fn abs n =
  if n < 0 then -n
  else n

fn main =
  println (abs 5)    # 5
  println (abs (-3)) # 3

Lambdas

\x -> x + 1
\x y -> x + y

Recursion

fn factorial n =
  if n == 0 then 1
  else n * factorial (n - 1)

# Mutual recursion works automatically
fn isEven n =
  if n == 0 then True
  else isOdd (n - 1)

fn isOdd n =
  if n == 0 then False
  else isEven (n - 1)

fn main =
  println (factorial 10)
  println (isEven 4)

Types

Primitive Types

Int         # 64-bit integer
Float       # 64-bit float
Bool        # True or False
Char        # Single character
String      # Immutable string
()          # Unit type

Sum Types (ADTs)

type Option a = Some a | None
type List a = Cons a (List a) | Nil
type Result a b = Ok a | Err b
type Expr = Num Int | Add Expr Expr | Mul Expr Expr

Record Types

type Point = { x : Int, y : Int }
type Person = { name : String, age : Int }

Tuple Types

(1, "hello")         # (Int, String)
(1, 2, 3)            # (Int, Int, Int)

Function Types

Int -> Int             # Function from Int to Int
Int -> Int -> Int      # Curried function
(a -> b) -> List a -> List b  # Higher-order function

Pattern Matching

Basic Match

match x
  | 0 => "zero"
  | 1 => "one"
  | _ => "other"

Constructor Matching

match xs
  | Cons x rest => x + sum rest
  | Nil => 0

Nested Patterns

match xs
  | Cons x (Cons y rest) => x + y
  | Cons x Nil => x
  | Nil => 0

Record Patterns

match person
  | { name, age } => name ++ " is " ++ Int.toString age

Wildcard Patterns

match x
  | Cons _ _ => "non-empty list"
  | Nil => "empty list"

Control Flow

If-Then-Else

if x > 0 then "positive"
else if x < 0 then "negative"
else "zero"

Multi-line If

if x > 0 then
  let y = x * 2
  y + 1
else
  0

Match as Expression

let description = match x
  | 0 => "zero"
  | _ => "non-zero"

Let Bindings

let x = 42
let y = x + 1
let (a, b) = (1, 2)           # Tuple destructuring
let { name, age } = person    # Record destructuring

Nested Let

let x = 1 in
let y = 2 in
x + y

References (Mutation)

let r = ref 0         # Create mutable reference
!r                    # Dereference (read)
r := !r + 1           # Update (write)

# No-arg lambdas use a wildcard parameter
let get = \ _ -> !r
get 0                 # Call with any value (unit)

Example: Counter

fn main =
  let r = ref 0
  let increment = \ _ -> r := !r + 1
  let get = \ _ -> !r
  increment 0
  increment 0
  println (get 0)  # 2

Modules and Imports

Import

import std.math.{add, mul}
import std.list as L
import std.{String, Int}

Module Declarations

package std.math

pub fn add x y = x + y

Selective Import

import std.math.{add}
add 1 2  # 3

Inspect (Debug Print)

inspect 42           # Int: 42
inspect 3.14         # Float: 3.14
inspect True         # Bool: True
inspect "hello"      # String: hello
inspect [1, 2, 3]    # [1, 2, 3]  (list sugar)
inspect (Cons 1 Nil) # [1]        (list sugar)
inspect Nil          # []         (list sugar)

Compile-Time Evaluation

Comptime Functions

comptime fn factorial n =
  if n == 0 then 1 else n * factorial (n - 1)

let x = factorial 10  # Evaluated at compile time

Comptime Expressions

let x = comptime 2 + 3  # Evaluated at compile time

Example Programs

Hello World

fn main =
  println "Hello, World!"

Fibonacci

fn fib n =
  if n <= 1 then n
  else fib (n - 1) + fib (n - 2)

fn main =
  println (fib 10)

Factorial

fn factorial n =
  if n == 0 then 1
  else n * factorial (n - 1)

fn main =
  println (factorial 10)

List Sum

type List a = Cons a (List a) | Nil

fn sum xs =
  match xs
    | Cons x rest => x + sum rest
    | Nil => 0

fn main =
  let xs = Cons 1 (Cons 2 (Cons 3 Nil))
  println (sum xs)

Map and Filter

type List a = Cons a (List a) | Nil

fn map f xs =
  match xs
    | Cons x rest => Cons (f x) (map f rest)
    | Nil => Nil

fn filter pred xs =
  match xs
    | Cons x rest =>
      if pred x then Cons x (filter pred rest)
      else filter pred rest
    | Nil => Nil

fn main =
  let xs = Cons 1 (Cons 2 (Cons 3 (Cons 4 Nil)))
  let doubled = map (\x -> x * 2) xs
  let evens = filter (\x -> x % 2 == 0) xs
  inspect doubled
  inspect evens

Pattern Matching

type Expr = Num Int | Add Expr Expr | Mul Expr Expr

fn eval expr =
  match expr
    | Num n => n
    | Add a b => eval a + eval b
    | Mul a b => eval a * eval b

fn main =
  let expr = Add (Num 1) (Mul (Num 2) (Num 3))
  println (eval expr)

Compiler Usage

ko --run file.ko           # JIT execute
ko file.ko                 # Dump LLVM IR
ko --emit-ir out.ll file.ko    # Write LLVM IR to file
ko --emit-obj out.o file.ko    # Emit object file
ko --emit-exe out file.ko      # Emit linked executable
ko --repl                   # Interactive REPL
ko --version                # Show version
